$comment: C99 6.7.6.2 + 6.7.7p2 (D-CSUBSET-VLA): an ARRAY whose ELEMENT type comes from a typedef carrying a runtime bound — `typedef int R[n]; R a[m];` — plus its fixed-alias sibling `typedef int R5[5]; R5 c[k];`. Both were EXCLUDED by the C4b typedef gate (`declTy == headTy` admitted only the suffix-less `R a;`), and both are compiled AND RUN by gcc 13.3.0 and clang 18.1.3 (probed separately, -std=c17 -Wall -Wextra, 2026-09-01), so the reference disjunction requires them. The hard part is that the object's TYPE has more array levels than its DECLARATOR has bounds: the missing level's size belongs to the typedef, which froze it once (6.7.7p2), so the object's size is a COMPOSITION of its own bound over that frozen value. Three witnesses carry the weight: (A) FREEZE-ONCE ACROSS THE COMPOSITION — `n` is mutated to 100 between the typedef and the object, so `sizeof a` must stay 24 and the row stride 12; a composition that re-lowered `n` would reserve 800 and stride by 400 (returns 1/2); (B) OFF-DIAGONAL — a[1][0] vs a[0][2] are distinct cells, so a stride taken from the wrong level aliases or transposes them (returns 3..8); (C) THE FIXED-ALIAS ARM — R5 froze nothing (compile-time size), so the seam is seeded by a constant instead of a copied slot, a different arm of the same code (returns 9..12). main is a LEAF (no calls) — the C1b VLA frame-model scope, since a VLA function that calls anything is separately refused (L_VlaNonLeafFrameUnsupported). `volatile` defeats const-folding so every bound is genuinely runtime. The `release` arm proves the frozen and composed size slots survive the full optimizer rather than being folded away. exitCode 42; returns 1..12 are the strict in-program pins. Red-on-disable: revert the semantic origin gate to `declTy == headTy` and (A)/(B) stop compiling; remove the fixed-sub-spine seam in computeVlaByteSize and (C) stops compiling.
